title: If … then
title_target: Om jag vann en miljon, skulle jag köpa en ny gitarr.
goal: Talk about real conditions and daydreams — *Om jag vinner…* versus *Om jag vann, skulle jag…* — with the right word order.
bekal: you can make real conditions with *om* + present tense
you can talk about dreams and unlikely situations with *om* + past and *skulle* + base form
you can give advice with *Om jag var du…* and ask politely with *Skulle du kunna…?*
wave: Go back to Unit 2: reread three of the *när*-sentences and turn them into *om*-sentences. Notice the difference: *när* means it will happen, *om* means it might.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Trisslotten
dialogs.intro: Friday night in the flat on Södermalm. Jonas comes home from the corner shop waving a scratch card — a *Trisslott* — and the three flatmates start dreaming out loud.

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Titta, jag har köpt en trisslott. Om jag vinner, bjuder jag på middag.
lines.id: Look, I've bought a scratch card. If I win, dinner's on me.
lines.literal: look, I have bought a Triss-ticket. if I win, treat I on dinner.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Det sa du förra gången också. Och då vann du tjugofem kronor.
lines.id: You said that last time too. And then you won twenty-five kronor.
lines.literal: that said you last time-the also. and then won you twenty-five crowns.

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Ja, men om jag vinner en miljon den här gången, så får ni följa med till Thailand.
lines.id: Yes, but if I win a million this time, then you can come along to Thailand.
lines.literal: yes, but if I win a million this here time-the, so get you follow with to Thailand.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Vad skulle du göra om du vann en miljon på riktigt?
lines.id: What would you do if you won a million for real?
lines.literal: what would you do if you won a million on real?

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Om jag vann en miljon, skulle jag köpa en ny gitarr och spela in ett album.
lines.id: If I won a million, I'd buy a new guitar and record an album.
lines.literal: if I won a million, would I buy a new guitar and play in an album.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Och jag skulle sluta jobba en månad och bara läsa böcker.
lines.id: And I'd stop working for a month and just read books.
lines.literal: and I would stop work a month and only read books.

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Men du jobbar på ett bibliotek!
lines.id: But you work in a library!
lines.literal: but you work on a library!

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Jag lånar ut böcker. Det är inte samma sak som att läsa dem.
lines.id: I lend books out. That's not the same thing as reading them.
lines.literal: I lend out books. that is not same thing as to read them.

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Och du, Dian? Vad skulle du göra?
lines.id: And you, Dian? What would you do?
lines.literal: and you, Dian? what would you do?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Om jag vann, skulle jag flyga hem till Indonesien och ta med hela familjen hit till midsommar.
lines.id: If I won, I'd fly home to Indonesia and bring my whole family here for midsummer.
lines.literal: if I won, would I fly home to Indonesia and take with whole family-the here to midsummer.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Vad fint! Men om de kom hit i juni, skulle de frysa.
lines.id: How lovely! But if they came here in June, they'd freeze.
lines.literal: how fine! but if they came here in June, would they freeze.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Då skulle jag köpa tjocka tröjor till alla. Problemet är löst!
lines.id: Then I'd buy thick sweaters for everyone. Problem solved!
lines.literal: then would I buy thick sweaters to all. problem-the is solved!

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Okej, nu skrapar jag. Om det står tre lika belopp, vinner jag.
lines.id: OK, now I'm scratching. If it shows three matching amounts, I win.
lines.literal: okay, now scratch I. if it stands three same amounts, win I.

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Tjugofem kronor. Igen. Men om jag köper en lott till, så…
lines.id: Twenty-five kronor. Again. But if I buy one more ticket, then…
lines.literal: twenty-five crowns. again. but if I buy a ticket more, so…

notes: **Om jag vinner, bjuder jag på middag** — a **real** condition, something that can actually happen: present tense in both halves, just like English "If I win, I'll…". Swedish doesn't even need *ska* here. *Bjuda på* (**BYÜ-dah poh**) = to treat (someone) to, to pay for: *Jag bjuder!* = It's on me!

**…, så får ni följa med** — after an *om*-clause, you can add *så* ("then") at the start of the main clause. It's optional and very common in speech. The verb still comes right after it: *så **får** ni*, not *så ni får*.

**Vad skulle du göra om du vann…?** — an **unreal** or unlikely condition: past tense after *om* (*vann*), and *skulle* (**SKÜL-leh**) + base form in the main clause. *Skulle* is English "would". The past tense here has nothing to do with past time — *om jag vann* means "if I won (now, some day)".

**Om jag vinner** or **om jag vann**? It depends on how likely you think it is. Jonas, ever the optimist, says *om jag vinner*. Dian, the realist, says *om jag vann*. English works the same way: "if I win" vs "if I won".

**Jag lånar ut böcker** — *låna* means "to borrow", *låna ut* (stress on the particle: **LOH-nah ÜT**) means "to lend". English needs two verbs; Swedish adds a particle — another particle verb for your list from Unit 3. *Kan du låna ut din cykel?* = Can you lend me your bike?

**Trisslott** (**TRIS-lot**) — *Triss* is Sweden's best-known scratch card, sold in every corner shop. You *skrapa* (**SKRAH-pah**, scratch) the boxes, and three matching *belopp* (**beh-LOP**, amounts) win. Many Swedes get one in their Christmas stocking. **Nå?** (**noh**) = "Well? So?" — impatient and curious.

grammars.title: Real or unreal?
body: Every *om*-sentence makes a choice: is this something that can really happen, or am I imagining? The tense after *om* signals that choice.

head: Type
Om-clause
Main clause
Example
rows: Om jag vinner, **bjuder** jag på middag.
Om jag **vann**, **skulle** jag köpa en gitarr.
Om jag **var** du, **skulle** jag ringa henne.

after: Use the ordinary past of every verb after *om*: *om jag hade tid* (had), *om vi bodde i Göteborg* (lived), *om hon kom* (came). There's no special form to learn.
"If I were you" is simply *Om jag var du*. (You will also meet the older form *vore* — *om jag vore du* — in writing; you'll practice it at B2.)
Imagining what would have happened in the past (*if I had known…*) is a B1 topic — for now, stick to the present and future.

grammars.title: Word order: om first or om last
body: The *om*-clause can come first or last. If it comes first, the whole clause counts as the first element of the sentence, so the main verb must come **right after it** — the verb-second rule at work.

head: Order
Example
rows: Jag **bjuder** på middag om jag vinner.
Om jag vinner, **bjuder** jag på middag.
Om jag vinner, så **bjuder** jag på middag.
Om det **inte regnar**, går vi ut.

after: The *om*-clause is a subordinate clause, so BIFF applies: *om du **inte** har tid*, *om jag **aldrig** vinner*.
A comma after the *om*-clause is common and makes long sentences easier to read, but it is not required.

head: Svenska
English
rows: Om jag var du, skulle jag…
If I were you, I would…
Jag skulle vilja ha en kaffe.

blocks.text: **Skulle** is also the key to Swedish politeness. *Jag vill ha en kaffe* is fine among friends, but *Jag skulle vilja ha en kaffe* is what you say to a stranger — just like "I'd like" instead of "I want". And *Skulle du kunna…?* turns any request into a gentle question.

blocks.title: Advice, two ways
items: *Du borde ringa henne.* — You should call her. (Unit 11: direct)
*Om jag var du, skulle jag ringa henne.* — If I were you, I'd call her. (softer: you put yourself in their shoes)
*Det kanske vore bra att ringa henne?* — Maybe it would be good to call her? (the softest — a preview of B2)

blocks.text: In a country that likes to keep things *lagom*, dreaming big is a slightly private affair. Ask a Swede what they'd do with a million and the answer is often modest: pay off the mortgage, fix the summer cottage, and maybe — just maybe — *resa jorden runt*.

blocks.title: Spiral review — back to Unit 11
items: Turn rules into conditions: *Om du inte behöver jobba på söndag, kan vi åka till Uppsala.*
*Om jag slapp jobba imorgon, skulle jag sova till tolv.*
Make two sentences of your own with *om* + *behöver inte*, *slipper* or *brukar*.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the right form of the word in brackets. Real condition or dream?
items: Om jag ____ rik, skulle jag resa jorden runt. (vara)
Om jag vann en miljon, ____ jag köpa ett hus. (would)
Om du ____ mer tid, vad skulle du göra? (ha)
Om det ____ imorgon, stannar vi hemma. (regna)
Om jag ____ du, skulle jag ringa henne. (vara)
Om vi ____ tåget nu, hinner vi. (ta)

exercises.prompt: Turn these real conditions into dreams: *Om jag vinner, köper jag…* becomes *Om jag vann, skulle jag köpa…*
items: Om jag vinner, köper jag en gitarr.
Om hon kommer, blir jag glad.
Om vi har tid, åker vi till Uppsala.
Om det är varmt, badar vi.
Om du frågar Maja, hjälper hon dig.

vad / skulle / du / göra / om / du / vann

om / det / inte / regnar / går / vi / ut

answers: var — skulle — hade — regnar — var — tar

Om jag vann, skulle jag köpa en gitarr. — Om hon kom, skulle jag bli glad. — Om vi hade tid, skulle vi åka till Uppsala. — Om det var varmt, skulle vi bada. — Om du frågade Maja, skulle hon hjälpa dig.
Om jag vinner, bjuder jag på middag. — Vad skulle du göra om du vann? — Om jag var du, skulle jag sova. — Om det inte regnar, går vi ut. — Om du vill, så kan vi ses.

Om jag vinner, bjuder jag alla på middag. — Vad skulle du göra om du vann en miljon? — Om jag var du, skulle jag sluta. — Om de kom hit i juni, skulle de frysa. — Om du inte har tid, kan vi ses imorgon. — Skulle du kunna hjälpa mig?
